# Pitloom's catalogued messages: URL credentials

See also: `messages.md` (the index of every code), `../SKILL.md` (which holds
the rule: explain and relay, never run the fix).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_message_reference.py; do not edit. -->

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of
each `<name>`, after at most one prefix: the index lists the prefixes and
`messages-values.md` the values.

## Codes

| Code | Level | Means | Since |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`credentials-unsafe`](#credentials-unsafe) | WARNING | A URL-typed value the SBOM states (a dependency's direct URL, a project URL, a download location) holds what may be a credential only: a query parameter named code, session, ticket, sid or otp, another whose name ends in _key, or a user name alone on an ssh or git URL (git@). Pitloom never rewrites a value: one that holds a credential is warned of (credentials-unsafe/written) or, in the refuse mode, refused (credentials-unsafe/refused) unless the user accepts that value by its fingerprint; one that may be a credential only, common in example and OAuth URLs, is warned of in either mode. | 0.25.0 |

### `credentials-unsafe`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A URL-typed value the SBOM states (a dependency's direct URL, a
  project URL, a download location) holds what may be a credential only: a query
  parameter named code, session, ticket, sid or otp, another whose name ends in
  _key, or a user name alone on an ssh or git URL (git@). Pitloom never rewrites
  a value: one that holds a credential is warned of (credentials-unsafe/written)
  or, in the refuse mode, refused (credentials-unsafe/refused) unless the user
  accepts that value by its fingerprint; one that may be a credential only,
  common in example and OAuth URLs, is warned of in either mode.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Did not refuse the value: the SBOM is written with it as
  written, unless another value is refused (credentials-unsafe/refused), which
  refuses the whole SBOM; said once per value of each SBOM, shown masked.
  Nothing is removed or rewritten.
- **Tell the user**: which value, as the line shows it, and that the SBOM states
  it as written. They check that the parameter or the ssh user name is no
  credential; if it is one, they remove it from the source and generate again,
  and rotate it, since a credential in a project's files is also in its history.
  Do not edit their files; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds a code, session, ticket, sid, otp or other _key parameter or an ssh user name; the SBOM states it as written [credentials-unsafe]
  ```

### `credentials-unsafe/accepted`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A URL-typed value the SBOM states holds what reads as a credential,
  and the user accepted it by its fingerprint (--accept-url-credential,
  accept-url-credentials in [tool.pitloom], the library's
  CredentialPolicy(accepted=...)), in either mode.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Did not refuse the value: the SBOM is written with it as
  written, unless another value is refused (credentials-unsafe/refused), which
  refuses the whole SBOM; said once per value of each SBOM, shown masked.
- **Tell the user**: which value the SBOM states as written, as the line shows
  it, and that anyone who reads the SBOM reads it too. If it is a real
  credential, they remove it from the source, rotate it and drop the acceptance.
  Do not edit their files or configuration; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds a credential that <fingerprint> accepts; the SBOM states it as written [credentials-unsafe/accepted]
  ```

### `credentials-unsafe/git-line-break`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: The user name or password of a Git URL holds a line break (an
  encoded %0A or %0D). A line break would add a line to what the credential
  helper hands git, so git could be told another value.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Fetched the URL without its credentials (a private repository
  then fails); said once per URL, shown masked.
- **Tell the user**: which URL, as the line shows it, and that its credentials
  were not used; a credential belongs in a .netrc file, a keyring (a git
  credential helper) or an environment variable, never in a URL. A credential
  typed into a command line is exposed in the shell history: they should
  consider it exposed and rotate it. Do not edit their files; ask first, and
  with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: URL=<url>: credentials holding a line break are not sent to git [credentials-unsafe/git-line-break]
  ```

### `credentials-unsafe/git-userinfo`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A Git URL holds user information (an @ before the first /) that
  Pitloom cannot split off the command line the way git reads it: a bracket or
  port that is not valid, an empty host, or an @ git reads as a password where
  the URL parser sees a query. Or the user name or password holds a NUL (an
  encoded %00), which cannot be handed to git at all.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Did not run git for the URL, and sent no request; the URL is
  shown masked.
- **Tell the user**: which URL, as the line shows it, and that it was not
  fetched; a credential belongs in a .netrc file, a keyring (a git credential
  helper) or an environment variable, never in a URL. They give the address
  without user information and run again. Do not edit their files; ask first,
  and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: user information cannot be taken out of the git command line; not fetched [credentials-unsafe/git-userinfo]
  ```

### `credentials-unsafe/http-clear`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A plain http:// Git URL holds a user name or password: git sends it
  to the server unencrypted, readable by anyone on the path.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Fetched the URL with its credentials, as asked; said once per
  URL, shown masked.
- **Tell the user**: which URL, as the line shows it, and that its credentials
  crossed the network in clear: they should use the https:// address and
  consider the credential exposed; a credential belongs in a .netrc file, a
  keyring (a git credential helper) or an environment variable, never in a URL.
  Do not edit their files; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: URL=<url>: credentials are sent in clear over http; use https [credentials-unsafe/http-clear]
  ```

### `credentials-unsafe/refused`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A URL-typed value the SBOM would state (a dependency's direct URL,
  a download location, a PURL, an external reference's locator) holds a user
  name or password, a query parameter named like a secret, an access token's
  shape, an scp-style address with a password, or a query nested or encoded too
  deeply to read, and the run is in the refuse mode (url-credentials = "refuse"
  in [tool.pitloom], --refuse-url-credentials, the library's
  CredentialPolicy(refuse=True)). An SBOM can be published, so it must not carry
  one. Each such value is one line naming the element and field that hold it and
  its fingerprint; the last line counts them and names no URL. Each line says
  how the surface that ran accepts the value: the command line's option, the
  build hook's [tool.pitloom] list, or the library's credentials argument.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote no SBOM: the command exits 1 (the Action step fails),
  the build hook fails the build, and the library raises ValueError carrying the
  code; 'embed-wheel --sbom' embeds nothing and leaves the wheel as it is, and
  loom.Run writes no fragment. Nothing is removed or rewritten.
- **Tell the user**: which value, as the line shows it, and where it is. First
  they remove the credential from the source and generate again; a credential in
  a project's files is also in its history, so they should consider it exposed
  and rotate it. Only once they have confirmed that one value is no secret (an
  example URL in a README) do they accept that value alone, the way the line
  gives with its fingerprint: --accept-url-credential, accept-url-credentials in
  [tool.pitloom] (also for the command line), the GitHub Action's
  accept-url-credentials input, or the library's credentials argument. Do not
  suggest turning the refuse mode off to get past it. Do not edit their files;
  ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: holds a credential (<element> <pointer>, <fingerprint>); remove it from the source, or accept this value with <option> <fingerprint> [credentials-unsafe/refused]
  ERROR: URL=<url>: holds a credential (<element> <pointer>, <fingerprint>); remove it from the source, or accept this value by listing it in [tool.pitloom] <setting> [credentials-unsafe/refused]
  ERROR: URL=<url>: holds a credential (<element> <pointer>, <fingerprint>); remove it from the source, or accept this value with credentials=CredentialPolicy(accepted=["<fingerprint>"]) [credentials-unsafe/refused]
  ERROR: <number> URL value(s) in the SBOM hold credentials; the SBOM is refused [credentials-unsafe/refused]
  ```

### `credentials-unsafe/registry`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A key or namespace given to the ID registry (an external reference
  URL), or the key or id of an SBOM element it would record, holds a user name
  or password, a query parameter named like a secret or an access token (also
  percent-encoded in a PURL qualifier), or a query nested too deeply to read (a
  value with more than 16 ?) or a PURL qualifier encoded too deeply to read
  (still encoded after five decodes). The registry file stores a key, an id and
  its namespace as written. A key given (register, 'loom id generate -e') and a
  registry file's entry follow the run's url-credentials mode; a namespace is
  refused in either mode.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: In the refuse mode, refused the key and stored nothing
  (error), or did not load a registry file with an entry holding one, left it as
  it is and stopped the run (error naming the file). In the warn mode, the
  default, stored the key as written, or loaded the file as it is (warning). A
  namespace holding one is refused in either mode (error). An SBOM element whose
  key or id holds one is left out of the registry in either mode, and the rest
  written (warning). A run whose SBOM is already built that reads the file again
  to save, in the refuse mode, says the refusal as a warning: nothing is saved
  and the SBOM stands.
- **Tell the user**: which value, as the line shows it. For an error, they give
  the value without the credential and run again; a credential typed on a
  command line is exposed in their shell history. For a warning, the value came
  from an SBOM ('loom id import'), the run's own data or their registry file:
  that element has no stable id (a new one is minted next run), and a credential
  in a shared SBOM, a project's files or a committed registry file is exposed,
  in its history too. For a line naming an ID registry file, they remove that
  entry from the file themselves and run again. A key the registry stores as
  written is in the registry file, and in its history once committed. Either way
  they should rotate it. Do not edit their registry file; ask first, and with
  nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: holds user information, a secret query value or an access token, or a query nested or encoded too deeply to read; an ID registry key is stored as written, so it is refused [credentials-unsafe/registry]
  ERROR: URL=<url>: holds user information, a secret query value or an access token, or a query nested or encoded too deeply to read; an ID registry namespace is stored as written, so it is refused [credentials-unsafe/registry]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds user information, a secret query value or an access token, or a query nested or encoded too deeply to read; the ID registry stores an element's key and id as written, so the element is skipped [credentials-unsafe/registry]
  ERROR: URL=<url>: holds user information, a secret query value or an access token, or a query nested or encoded too deeply to read; ID registry file '<path>' is not loaded; remove the entry [credentials-unsafe/registry]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds user information, a secret query value or an access token, or a query nested or encoded too deeply to read; ID registry file '<path>' is loaded as it is; remove the entry [credentials-unsafe/registry]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds user information, a secret query value or an access token, or a query nested or encoded too deeply to read; the ID registry stores the key as written [credentials-unsafe/registry]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds user information, a secret query value or an access token, or a query nested or encoded too deeply to read; ID registry file '<path>' is not loaded; remove the entry [credentials-unsafe/registry]
  ```

### `credentials-unsafe/written`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A URL-typed value the SBOM states (a dependency's direct URL, a
  download location, a PURL, an external reference's locator) holds a user name
  or password, a query parameter named like a secret, an access token's shape,
  an scp-style address with a password, or a query nested or encoded too deeply
  to read, and the run is in the warn mode, the default (Pitloom runs in CI and
  build hooks and does not fail them by default). Each such value is one line
  naming the element and field that hold it and its fingerprint, and how the
  surface that ran turns the refuse mode on: the command line's
  --refuse-url-credentials, the build hook's [tool.pitloom] url-credentials, or
  the library's credentials argument.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote the SBOM with the value as written: the command exits
  0, the build hook does not fail the build, and the library returns. Said once
  per value of each SBOM, shown masked. Nothing is removed or rewritten.
- **Tell the user**: which value, as the line shows it, and where it is, and
  that the SBOM now carries the credential: anyone who reads the SBOM reads it,
  and it is also in the project's files and their history, so they should
  consider it exposed, rotate it and remove it from the source, then generate
  again. Offer to turn on url-credentials = "refuse" in [tool.pitloom]
  (--refuse-url-credentials on the command line, url-credentials: refuse on the
  GitHub Action) so that CI refuses such an SBOM from then on. Only once they
  have confirmed that one value is no secret (an example URL in a README) do
  they accept that value alone by its fingerprint (--accept-url-credential,
  accept-url-credentials in [tool.pitloom], the GitHub Action's
  accept-url-credentials input), which quiets this line. Do not edit their
  files; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds a credential (<element> <pointer>, <fingerprint>); the SBOM states it as written; remove it from the source, or refuse such values with <option> [credentials-unsafe/written]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds a credential (<element> <pointer>, <fingerprint>); the SBOM states it as written; remove it from the source, or refuse such values with [tool.pitloom] <setting> = "refuse" [credentials-unsafe/written]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: holds a credential (<element> <pointer>, <fingerprint>); the SBOM states it as written; remove it from the source, or refuse such values with credentials=CredentialPolicy(refuse=True) [credentials-unsafe/written]
  ```
